Product acceptance guidance: Codex ↔ Claude Code harness full alignment
User-facing reliability promise after complete alignment
After complete alignment, users should be able to rely on the Codex harness as a durable operational equivalent of the Claude Code harness for workflow behavior, not merely a partial port.
Users should be able to expect:
1. 
Same workflow state semantics
• 
/dev and /redev state ownership is Codex-native.
• 
State survives session restarts where Claude Code state would survive.
• 
Re-entry, continuation, cancellation, and completion behave consistently.
2. 
Same lifecycle enforcement
• 
Prompt, pre-action, post-action, stop, and subagent-stop events fire at the same user-visible decision points.
• 
Blocking hooks actually block.
• 
Warnings are distinguishable from hard failures.
• 
Stop/subagent-stop checks cannot be bypassed by normal workflow completion.
3. 
Same safety posture
• 
Commands/actions prohibited in Claude Code must be prohibited or fail closed in Codex.
• 
Any unsupported enforcement surface must not silently pass.
• 
“Best effort” safety is not acceptable for a full-alignment claim.
4. 
Same compatibility inventory outcome
• 
No remaining imported, fallback, or unsupported compatibility classes for behavior that affects user-visible workflow, state, lifecycle, safety, or release gating.
• 
If a class cannot be implemented because Codex lacks a required runtime primitive, that must be explicitly reported as a runtime impossibility, not hidden as compatibility.
5. 
Same release gating expectations
• 
A user should not have to know whether they are running under Claude Code or Codex to know whether /dev, /redev, checkpoints, hooks, lifecycle checks, and blocking rules are enforced.
• 
If parity cannot be guaranteed, the product must say so before the user starts the workflow.
Required wording for runtime impossibility
Runtime impossibilities must be phrased plainly and specifically.
Acceptable wording:
This workflow behavior cannot be fully aligned in the Codex harness because Codex does not expose <specific runtime primitive>. The Codex harness therefore fails closed for <affected action/event> instead of silently continuing. This is not full Claude Code parity.
For user-facing command output:
Cannot continue: this /redev path requires Claude Code-compatible <event/hook/state capability>, but the Codex runtime cannot provide it. No workflow state was advanced. Use Claude Code for this workflow or remove the requirement for full alignment.
For compatibility inventory:
json
{
  "class": "runtime_impossible",
  "capability": "<specific capability>",
  "reason": "Codex runtime does not expose <specific primitive>",
  "user_impact": "<what the user cannot rely on>",
  "behavior": "fail_closed",
  "release_claim_allowed": false
}

Download
Do not use vague wording like:
• 
“Partially supported”
• 
“Best effort”
• 
“Fallback available”
• 
“Equivalent enough”
• 
“Unsupported but safe”
• 
“Handled by native implementation”
Those phrases hide risk from the user.
Must block release
Release must be blocked if any of the following remain true:
1. 
Compatibility inventory still reports `imported`, `fallback`, or `unsupported` classes
• 
Especially for lifecycle, workflow state, hook enforcement, subagent-stop behavior, checkpointing, or safety controls.
2. 
Any Claude Code safety rule silently degrades
• 
A blocked Claude Code action must not become a warning or no-op in Codex unless explicitly accepted as non-parity.
3. 
Lifecycle events are not semantically equivalent
• 
It is not enough that event names exist.
• 
They must fire at the same effective workflow moments and have the same blocking consequences.
4. 
State ownership is split or ambiguous
• 
Codex-native state must be authoritative for Codex workflows.
• 
Imported Claude artifacts may be reference data, but not hidden sources of truth.
5. 
Fallback behavior can advance workflow state
• 
If Codex cannot enforce a required behavior, it must fail closed before mutating workflow state.
6. 
Subagent-stop or stop enforcement is weaker than Claude Code
• 
Workflow completion must not bypass pending checkpoint, quality, or lifecycle obligations.
7. 
User-visible commands claim full alignment while exceptions remain
• 
The release may not say “fully aligned,” “Claude-compatible,” or “durable parity” if any runtime impossibility or unsupported class remains.
8. 
No durable regression test proves parity
• 
Alignment must be protected by tests or checks that fail when compatibility classes reappear or lifecycle semantics drift.
Product acceptance standard
A release is acceptable only when the user can truthfully be told:
The Codex harness now enforces the same /dev and /redev workflow contract as the Claude Code harness for state ownership, lifecycle events, blocking behavior, safety gates, and completion semantics. Any behavior Codex cannot represent fails closed and is explicitly reported before workflow state advances.
If that sentence is not true, the release should be blocked.
